method: Complete reads of three pinned source/header files, Git blob and SHA256 validation. No new hash-vector execution in this audit.
findings: Public header declares sequential, parallel and XOF variants and uses packed parameter blocks with compile-time size checks. Declarations do not establish runtime coverage of unread implementations.

Endian helpers use memcpy only under explicit NATIVE_LITTLE_ENDIAN; otherwise assemble/store little-endian bytes, including16/32/48/64-bit helpers. secure_zero_memory calls volatile memset function pointer.

BLAKE2b initializes output length1..64 and optional key1..64, sets sequential fanout/depth and clears salt/personal fields. init_param directly loads supplied parameter bytes without full validation; it is a lower-level caller contract.

Update keeps final full128-byte block buffered by using strict greater-than comparisons, maintains128-bit byte counter with carry and ignores zero input length. Final rejects null/small output and repeated finalization, zero-pads buffer and serializes digest before clearing temporary buffer.

One-shot entry validates pointers and lengths, initializes, updates and finalizes. Update/final results are not propagated after initialization. With validated ordinary inputs this alone does not establish reachable failure; no runtime bug claimed.
Selftest conditional requires blake2-kat.h, which is absent from pinned tree inventory. Existing selftest source therefore is not evidence that this imported package ran its original vectors.
limits: No independent BLAKE2b oracle result yet; implementation review only.
